title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC moral head; head-ratio ≠ immediate imputation
pass_a_gloss: PLAC: Did he imagine I meant a literal physical head, though I expressly named an improper or moral body like a commonwealth? A commonwealth is not a physical body; still, no one calls a private man the commonwealth's head before the commonwealth exists, nor calls today's state the body of a prince dead for centuries. That political head and body is my meaning. Apart from that I never denied Adam is head of the race in the learned man's present sense. Yet how does that head-account secure immediate imputation of Adam's sin? Was he head in that sense only while sinning? Does Abraham's headship of the Jews mean some one act of Abraham is charged that way to every Jew?
pass_b_english: PLAC. Did the learned man think I had so lost my mind as to understand a head properly so called, when I said in express words an improperly so called, or moral, body, as a republic? For it is plain that a republic is not a physical body. And yet, although nature has not bound a republic to its kingly or magisterial head by nerves and ties, no one would say that a man was then head of the republic when he himself lived as a private person, the republic not yet born; nor will the republic which now is be called the body of that prince who a hundred or a thousand years ago ceased to be among the living. Such a head, such a political body, I understood. For otherwise I do not deny, nor have I ever denied, that Adam is the head of the human race in that sense which the learned man explains in this place. But what does that account of the head do for the immediate imputation of Adam's sin? Was Adam head in that way only while he sinned? Or because Abraham was head of the Jewish people, is some action of his in that way imputed to all and each of the Jews?
source_text: PLAC. Putavitne Vir Doctus me ita insanivisse ut caput proprie dictum intellexerim, qui disertis verbis dixi corpus improprie dictum, seu morale, tanquam rempublicam? Manifestum enim est rempublicam non esse corpus physicum: Et tamen, quamvis natura rempublicam cum capite suo rege, vel magistratu non colligaverit nervis & vinculis, nemo dixerit hominem tunc fuisse caput reipublicae, cum ipse viveret privatus, nondum nata republica: neque respublica quae nunc est corpus dicetur illius principis, qui ante centum aut mille annos desiit esse in vivis. Tale caput, tale corpus politicum intellexi. Nam alioqui non nego, neque negavi unquam, quin sit Adamus caput generis humani eo sensu quem Vir doctus hoc loco exponit. Sed quid ad immediatam imputationem peccati Adamici facit ista capitis ratio? An sic caput fuit Adamus duntaxat dum peccavit? An propterea quod Abrahamus gentis Judaicae caput fuit, eo modo ejus aliqua actio omnibus & singulis Judaeis imputatur?
